newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank says August M3 grew annualised 8.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank says August M3 grew annualised 8.7 pct.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday that German M3 money supply grew at an annualised rate of 8.7 percent in August, up from 8.6 percent in July.
The growth was stronger than expected.
Most economists had predicted M3 growth would have slowed again in August, following a steady downward trend seen in recent months.

Economists had predicted an annualised rate of 8.0 percent from 8.6 percent in July. Forecasts ranged from 7.9 percent to 8.2 percent. The Bundesbank is aiming for M3 growth between four and seven percent this year.

German bonds dropped quickly in response to the figure on the assumption that it made a further cut in German interest rates less likely. There has been some speculation that a further cut in German rates was possible later this year.

Klaus Baader, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London told Reuters Financial Television: "The number is not a major catastrophe, but the process of rapid convergence toward the growth target (four to seven per cent) has been interrupted. Reaching the target after this will be an uphill struggle."
The Bundesbank targets M3 money supply growth as its main monetary policy indicator on the grounds that it provides a guide to future inflation.
